description.narrative: The development objective of the Human Capital Operation (HCO) for Ethiopia is to improve learning outcomes and nutrition services for girls and boys, and to strengthen service delivery and accountability, in all regions including areas affected by conflict, droughts and high levels of refugees. The HCO will have three components. Component 1 using Program-for-Results (PforR) will support basic service delivery at the woreda level, including for refugees and host communities; component 2 using investment project financing (IPF) will improve human capital outcomes in areas affected by conflicts, droughts, and high level of refugees and strengthen system capacity, including on refugee integration and protection through technical assistance; and component 3 as a zero-dollar contingent emergency response component (CERC) that can be triggered to respond to emergencies if, and when, deemed appropriate.

condition.narrative: Financing Agreement (FA), Schedule 2, Section I.B.2 (a) The Recipient shall, not later than six (6) months after the EffectiveDate, prepare in accordance with terms of reference acceptable to the Association and furnish to the Association for prior review,a Project Operations Manual covering the matters listed in the FA.

Financing Agreement, Schedule 2, Section I.A.2 (a) The Recipient shall, through the MOF establish not later than four (4) monthsafter the Effective Date, and thereafter maintain, at all times during the implementation of the Operation: (A) technicalcommittees at the federal, regional and Woreda levels, with mandates, resources and functions satisfactory to the Association, tobe responsible for, inter alia, operational oversight, tracking performance, and strengthening inter-ministerial/bureau/officecoordination at their respective levels; and (B) a Steering Committee with a mandate, resources and functions satisfactory to theAssociation, to be responsible for, inter alia, prompt and efficient oversight and implementation of activities under Operation.

Financing Agreement, Schedule 2, Section I.B.3 (a) The Recipient shall, not later than five (5) months after the Effective Date,(and thereafter by March 31 of each subsequent EFY) prepare and furnish to the Association, a work plan and budget containing allactivities proposed for implementation in the following calendar year including: (i) a detailed timetable for the sequencing andimplementation of said activities; (ii) the types of expenditures required for such activities, including a proposed financingplan; and (iii) a budget establishing the proposed amounts and sources of financing.

Financing Agreement, Schedule 2, Section I.D The Recipient shall ensure that all counterpart funds so allocated shall be usedexclusively to pay for said domestic Eligible Expenditures under the Project. For the avoidance of doubt, the counterpart fundsallocation for said domestic Eligible Expenditures, shall be determined using the following formula: For each Dollar allocated bythe Association for financing said domestic Eligible Expenditures, the Recipient shall allocate 50 percent of the Ethiopian Birrequivalent using the prevailing official exchange rate; or such other formula as may be determined by the Association from time totime and agreed upon with the Recipient during the implementation of the Project. The Recipient shall ensure that all suchallocated counterpart funds shall be used exclusively to pay for said domestic Eligible Expenditures.

Financing Agreement, Schedule 2, Section V.1 T1. The Recipient shall, at all times during the implementation of the Operation,ensure that Woreda-level GPG allocations, on average, for basic services sectors (education, health, agriculture, water and ruralroads) at the regional levels (excluding Addis Ababa) shall not decline year on year from the baseline of 64 percent in EFY2015, asagreed upon with the Association.

Financing Agreement, Schedule 2, Section V.2 The Recipient shall, no later than four (4) months after the Effective Date: (a)(i)prepare, in form and substance satisfactory to the Association, assessments at the federal, regional and Woreda levels to: (A)prioritize and tailor multisectoral interventions for each level; (B) review existing models and identification technologiessupport; and (C) identify capacity building needs and priorities at the Woreda level; and (ii) and thereafter adopt and implementthe recommendations of said assessments; and (b) develop, in form and substance satisfactory to the Association, a data collectioninstrument, and thereafter carry out collection of data for baseline indicators, in accordance with the provisions of saidinstrument.
